reader.title: Killing of Silas Jeffries and Abe Davis
bases: Armed friends of a murdered stockman hunted down and killed two neighbors suspected of leading the party that killed him, and the Washington Evening Star headlined it a 'lynching' (A1, A3, A4).

Jeffries and Davis were killed by Durant's armed 'friends', with no officer or legal process mentioned, because they were suspected of leading his murderers (A1, A3, A5); the number of killers is never given beyond the plural 'friends', so the three-or-more element rests on inference.
Every copy traces to one Little Rock dispatch of Nov. 19 (a Nov. 20 variant in A5), with no local or independent report (A1, A3, A4, A5).

summary.text: The killing of Silas Jeffries and Abe Davis was a reprisal killing near Tushomma, Indian Territory, in November 1888, in which armed friends of a murdered stockman, William Durant, hunted down and killed two neighbors suspected of leading the party that shot him.
Known only from a single Little Rock wire dispatch, the story ran in papers from Washington to Minnesota, and the Washington Evening Star headlined it as a lynching.
According to the Little Rock dispatch, Durant had been quarrelling with two neighbors named Davis and Jeffries.
On the Friday night before the dispatch, November 16, a party of men called him from his house near Tushomma and shot him in his yard, "riddling his body with bullets."
The killing "aroused his friends," who armed themselves and hunted down Silas Jeffries and Abe Davis, the two men suspected of having led the party that murdered Durant.
Both men were killed; the Savannah Morning News headline said they were shot.
The dispatch gave no date, place or witnesses for their deaths and did not say how many men took part.
No report of an inquest, arrests or prosecution of either Durant's killers or the men who killed Jeffries and Davis appears in the coverage.
The story entered the press as a Little Rock dispatch dated November 19, printed that day by the Washington Evening Star by way of Chicago and by the Alexandria Gazette under "A Brutal Murder."

Headline writers framed it in different ways: the Evening Star called it "the lynching of two of his supposed assassins," the Savannah Morning News wrote "Two Men Suspected of a Murder Shot by Avengers," and the Richmond Dispatch "Assassinated—Swift Metalliation [Retaliation]."

The St. Paul Daily Globe put the weight on the first killing, headlining "Desperadoes Take the Life of an Innocent Stockman," while the Camden Evening Telegram called the affair "An Indian Territory Vendetta."
Over the following week the item was cut down to a sentence or two in news summaries in Delaware, Tennessee, Kentucky, South Carolina, Pennsylvania, West Virginia and Connecticut.

Condensing introduced errors: a Clarksville and a Kentucky paper said the two were hunted down "by the neighbors," the Martinsburg Herald placed Durant's murder at Little Rock, and the Connecticut Western News described Jeffries and Davis as "of Little Rock, Ark."
No paper gave the race of anyone involved, and none commented editorially on the killings.
Most copies place Durant's home near Tushomma or Tushoma, but the Camden Evening Telegram, printing a version dated November 20, gave Tishomingo.
The same variant said the two were suspected of leading the party "to Durant's house" rather than the party that murdered him, a difference of wording that does not change the accusation.

accounts.label: Little Rock wire report
accounts.gist: Durant was shot in his yard by a party of men after quarrelling with neighbors Davis and Jeffries; his armed friends then hunted down and killed the two, who were suspected of having led that party.

accounts.label: Nov. 20 variant (Camden Telegram)
accounts.gist: The same story placed near Tishomingo, saying the friends 'have since' killed the two, suspected of having led the party to Durant's house.

framing.detail: The Washington Evening Star headed the dispatch 'Bloodshed in Indian Territory' and named the reprisal 'the lynching of two of his supposed assassins'.
Savannah's 'Shot by Avengers' and Richmond's 'Swift Metalliation [Retaliation]' cast the killers as avengers, while St. Paul called Durant 'an innocent stockman' and his killers 'desperadoes'.
Most papers ran the wire text unchanged or as a one-paragraph news-summary item, some under headings such as 'A Brutal Murder' and 'Two of the Assassins Killed'.

conflicts.note: Most copies of the Nov. 19 dispatch give Tushomma or Tushoma; only the Camden variant dated Nov. 20 gives Tishomingo, likely a substitution of a better-known name.

conflicts.note: Minor wording variant; both make the two suspects the leaders of Durant's killers.

record_check.dossier: 1888-11-16 is the Friday night Durant was killed; Jeffries and Davis were killed between then and the Nov. 19 dispatch, date not stated.
Two killed in the reprisal (Jeffries and Davis); the third death, Durant, is the triggering murder, not part of this episode.
Durant's armed 'friends'; no deputizing, officer or legal authority is mentioned.
Supported (Silas Jeffries and Abe Davis; 'Siras' in one copy).

record_check.record: said to have led the party that murdered Durant
record_check.dossier: Supported: suspected of having led the party that murdered Durant, after quarrelling with him.
The Little Rock wire ran in at least 13 white papers from Nov. 19 to Nov. 28.

info: Durant was killed 'Friday night last' (Nov. 16, 1888, by the Nov. 19 dateline); Jeffries and Davis were killed afterward and before the Nov. 19 dispatch, on no stated date.
Near Tushomma (Tushoma), Indian Territory; one copy gives Tishomingo, I.T.
Silas Jeffries (also 'Siras Jeffries') and Abe Davis, neighbors of Durant; race not stated.
Suspected of having led the party that murdered stockman William Durant; Durant had been quarrelling with them.
Durant's friends, who armed themselves; no names given.
